- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 70), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 2–5% below peak to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model lags in adjusting; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price volatility; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion and sentiment-driven noise.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.33/0.67 alternation, model exhibits oscillation bias; smooth forecast by averaging 2–3 prior values to reduce overfitting.
